title: 幾何論約·卷一~卷二 (vol 1)
shelf_note: Du Zhigeng's Chinese compendium of Euclid in a Siku Quanshu manuscript copy (the block heart reads 欽定四庫全書, 卷二). It belongs in a general/universal library collection of Chinese mathematical texts.
structure_note: The structure count pages_translated = 0 contradicts pages_translated_field = 107, and this page is translated, so the count looks like an instrument error (E2) and not missing translations. 107 of 112 pages have OCR. Siku leaves carry only 卷 numbers in the block heart and no folio numbers on the face, so only 6 pages have a printed number and the 2 backsteps and 2 repeats most likely come from juan markers or misread furniture, not from a scan splice. Published is 'Unknown', but the copy is from the Qianlong-era Siku Quanshu.

pages.printed_marker: none visible (block heart: "欽定四庫全書" … "卷二"; no leaf number)
pages.layout: single half-leaf, nine vertical ruled columns read right to left, in a manuscript copyist's hand; block-heart title and juan number in the right margin; no diagram

ocr_errors.problem: The OCR prints the Japanese shinjitai form 増 for the 增 written on the leaf, in all four places it occurs. Meaning is unchanged.

ocr_errors.image: 欽定四庫全書 … 卷二
ocr_errors.problem: The OCR leaves out the block-heart title and juan marker. This is harmless for the reading text but loses the locator.

other.note: The <meta> speculates that the opening 上方形 is 'presumably naming the square of the figure as a whole'. This is not on the page. It most likely completes 'square on [line X]' from the previous page, and the English just renders it as 'square.' The meta goes to the metadata box, not the reading text.

book_verdict: The page is the right leaf. The transcription is accurate apart from a variant character form, and the translation of the end of Elements II.5 and the opening of II.6 is faithful. Its notes are correct and useful: the gloss on 磬折形 and the 半兀 copying slip both check against the image. The only flag is a book-level count mismatch (pages_translated 0 vs 107).
